role.altitude: The electrical drafter keeps interpreting requirements, deciding changes, determining the service type and explaining drawings on site; comparing configurations line by line, retyping values, logging mailed requests and mailing revisions shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading comparison reports from design data
Checking extracted requirements against the sheet
role.ambitious_version: A drafter who spends the time on the questions the drawings raise, not on copying between them.

tasks.short: Open the schematic and element configuration, compare the logic element configuration with the engineering schematics, decide the change, calculate figures, modify the element, record the change and confirm it with the engineer.

steps.what: Drafter opens the engineering schematics and the element configuration on the display screen
Drafter compares the logic element configuration with the schematics item by item
Drafter decides whether to convert, redesign or modify the element
Drafter calculates figures such as ratings and values for the modified element, retyping inputs from the schematic
Drafter modifies the element in the design software
Drafter writes the change note with the differences and calculated figures
Drafter confirms the change with the engineer

tasks.design: Where the schematic and the element configuration live in the same electrical design system, a comparison report lists every connection and parameter that differs, and the drafter checks each difference instead of comparing item by item. A checked calculation template reads ratings and values from the design data instead of retyped inputs. The change note is filled with the differences and figures, and the drafter adds the reasons. Deciding the change, modifying the element and confirming with the engineer stay with the drafter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Configurations were compared by eye and values retyped into calculation sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Design systems that report differences and export parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy elements whose schematic exists only as a scan.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a difference was made on purpose.
tasks.altitude: Less comparing and retyping; the change decision stays.

reach.learn: Whether change notes list every difference.

evidence.claim: Electrical design software generates reports, wire lists and bills of materials from the design.
Comparing a configuration with its schematic is a deterministic report when both are in one data model.

assumptions: Boundary: comparing and modifying logic elements; drafting detail drawings (task 21951) and examining schematics to verify drafting specifications (task 21949) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: schematic and configuration in the same design system for about 60% of elements; s2 is priced at that share.
s4 saves retyping inputs from the schematic; s6 saves retyping differences and figures into the note.
Deciding, modifying and confirming keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of elements with schematics in the design system.
research_questions: Do missed differences found later fall?

incremental.description: Drafter keeps the calculation template checked.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: scanned legacy schematics; high: elements fully in the design system.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect requirement data from customer blueprints, interpret customer requirements, record them, look up wiring standards, and consult with the assembler regarding schematics, wiring procedures or conductor paths.

steps.what: Drafter collects title block data, requirement tables and notes from the customer blueprints

loop.output: Title block fields, tables and notes as a list, each linked to its sheet and position.
loop.check: The drafter checks every item against the sheet it came from.
loop.stop: Sheets the step cannot read are read by hand.

steps.what: Drafter reviews blueprints to determine customer requirements
Drafter types the requirements list into the project file
Drafter looks up the company wiring standards and earlier projects

loop.input: The drafter's question and the company's wiring standards and project documentation.
loop.output: An answer with links to the standard clauses or earlier drawings it used.
loop.check: The drafter opens each linked clause or drawing before use.
loop.stop: Questions without a linked source are looked up by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Standards and earlier projects are spread over many documents.

steps.what: Drafter consults with the assembler regarding schematics, wiring procedures or conductor paths
Drafter answers follow-up questions from the assembler by mail

tasks.design: An extraction step lists title block fields, requirement tables and notes from the customer blueprints, each linked to its sheet, and the drafter checks every item. The checked items become the requirements list instead of being typed again. An answer desk over the company wiring standards and project documents answers questions with links. Interpreting the requirements and consulting the assembler stay with the drafter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were read and typed out sheet by sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Extraction with sheet references and answers over verified documentation.
tasks.still_hard: Handwritten notes and old scanned blueprints.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which conductor path the assembler can actually build.
tasks.altitude: Less reading and typing; interpretation and consultation stay.

reach.learn: Whether wiring questions come back less often.

evidence.claim: An electrical design assistant answers questions from verified documentation.
A model can extract title blocks and tables from drawings.

assumptions: Boundary: reviewing blueprints and consulting the assembler; consulting engineers on design concepts (task 21947) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: customer blueprints delivered as vector files for about 60% of projects; s1 is priced at that share.
s3 saves typing items already extracted and checked in s1.
Interpreting and consulting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of customer blueprints that are scans.

incremental.description: Drafter keeps standards documents current for the answer desk.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: scanned blueprints; high: vector blueprints with tables.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive and log work order requests, study them, look up the installation's drawings, ask for missing information, determine the type of service such as lighting or power, record it and confirm with the engineer.

steps.what: Requester submits the work order request in a request form
Drafter logs mailed work order requests in the request list
Drafter studies the work order requests and attachments
Drafter searches the drawing library for the installation's existing drawings and load data
Drafter asks the requester for missing information
Drafter determines the type of service, such as lighting or power, and the load demanded by the installation
Drafter records the service type and scope on the work order
Drafter confirms the scope with the engineer

tasks.design: Requesters submit work orders through a request form with required fields for location, asset number, equipment and loads. The request lands in the queue instead of being logged by hand from mail. The asset number opens the installation's drawings in the drawing library, instead of the drafter searching by address. Required fields cut back-and-forth for missing data. Studying the request, determining the service type and confirming with the engineer stay with the drafter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by mail and drawings were searched by address.
tasks.enabler_now: Request forms with required fields linked to the drawing library.
tasks.still_hard: Requests for sites with no drawings on file.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a lighting request will really need new power.
tasks.altitude: Less logging and searching; the service decision stays.

evidence.claim: Records, logs and schedules suit a records app with notifications.

assumptions: Boundary: studying work orders; reviewing work orders and manuals with vendors (task 21958) and locating project files in the database library (task 21953) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2 and s5: requesters use the form for about 70% of requests; s2 and s5 are priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: asset numbers linked to drawings in the library for about 70% of installations; s4 is priced at that share.
s2 saves retyping mailed requests into the list.
s3 is priced low: structured fields help, but the drafter still reads every request.
Requesters' form time is shown in s1 and is about what their mail took.
unknowns: Share of installations with drawings linked to asset numbers.
research_questions: Is time from request to scope shorter?

incremental.description: Drafter links new drawings to asset numbers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mailed requests and unlinked drawings; high: form requests for linked assets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the drawing set, explain drawings to production or construction teams, answer questions, decide and draft adjustments, update the revision block, have the engineer approve, and issue the revised drawing.

steps.what: Drafter prepares the drawing set and marks points to explain
Drafter explains drawings to production or construction teams
Drafter answers questions from team members by mail and phone
Drafter decides on the adjustments needed
Drafter revises the drawings with the adjustments
Drafter types the revision block and the transmittal
Engineer checks and approves the final revised drawing
Drafter issues the revised drawing to the production or construction teams

approvals.approved_version: The revised drawing at the revision letter approved by the engineer in s7, issued to the teams on its transmittal list; any later change needs a new revision and approval.

tasks.design: Questions from the teams go into a shared question list linked to drawing sheets, so an answer given once reaches everyone on that sheet, instead of the same question coming by mail from several people. The document control system fills the revision block and transmittal from the change record. After the engineer approves the revision, the drafter publishes it to the teams' drawing portal, and the old revision is withdrawn, instead of PDFs mailed to each recipient. Explaining drawings, deciding adjustments and revising stay with the drafter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions and revised drawings went by individual mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared question lists and document control with transmittals.
tasks.still_hard: Teams on site without access to the portal.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a drawing so the team sees the risk in a cable route.
tasks.altitude: Fewer mails; explaining on site stays.

reach.learn: Whether they work from the current revision.

evidence.claim: Document control systems issue revisions with transmittals and withdraw superseded versions.

assumptions: Boundary: explaining drawings and adjusting them; conferring with engineering staff to resolve problems (task 21950) and reproducing drawings (task 21959) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3 and s8: teams use the question list and drawing portal on about 60% of projects; s3 and s8 are priced at that share.
s6 saves retyping revision data already in the change record; s8 saves mailing each recipient.
Engineer time is shown in s7 and does not change.
unknowns: Share of teams with portal access on site.
research_questions: Is work on superseded drawings less frequent?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few portal users; high: all teams on the portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
